title: transient-penalty-amortization-causes-per-key-rate-starvation
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Summary: The amortization heuristic that smooths burst penalties is incorrectly applied across shard/lease boundaries, resulting in persistent, skewed penalty application for a small set of API keys. Symptoms: those keys see sustained 429s and degraded throughput for minutes-to-hours after a transient burst; overall system token accounting appears consistent but enforcement is biased. Impact: customer-visible throttling (P1 incidents), regressions in latency SLOs for affected routes, and increased support tickets. This ticket captures root-cause analysis, proposed remediation, and rollout plan.
root_cause_analysis: When a primary lease moves between edge shards, the amortization state (amort_cursor and amort_bucket) is stored at shard granularity to reduce memory. During a lease handoff the receiving shard replays pending penalty amortization, but our replay path double-applies stale amortization records if the handoff overlap window is non-zero. Additionally, the fastpath enforcement path reads a transient global 'shard_penalty_epoch' instead of a per-key ledger, so keys that experienced the handoff see their remaining allowance clipped twice. The combination causes a subset of keys to be left with a negative effective allowance until the amortization window expires, manifesting as prolonged throttling. We confirmed the race in traces (trace IDs linked below) and saw consistent counterexamples in the shard handoff logs where amort_record_id was reprocessed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure small per-key burst window (e.g., 50 requests/min) and enable shard-lease churn in staging with synthetic clients tied to 10 keys.
2) Fire a burst from a single key and immediately trigger shard reallocation (force lease transfer) via repro tool.
3) Observe enforcement traces: the key receives initial penalty, then after transfer the same amort_record_id is applied again and the key hits 429s for the remainder of amort_window.
4) Confirm in metrics: per-key 429 rate spikes, per-shard penalty-apply logs show duplicate record processing.
5) Re-run with proposed fix toggled off/on to see difference in time-to-recover.
proposed_solution: 1) Move amortization ledger from shard-scoped aggregated buckets to a compact per-key amort_record index keyed by (org, key, route) with idempotency token and monotonic applied_version. 2) Ensure the lease handoff path uses the applied_version to avoid re-applying records during overlap windows. 3) Keep memory bounded via TTL + periodic compaction (LFU eviction) and compressed deltas for cold keys. 4) Add defensive check in fastpath: if amort_record.applied_version <= local_applied_version, skip. 5) Add a reconciliation job to compute and restore 'missing' allowance for keys that were left penalized due to previous double-application; by default the job will be opt-in for affected tenants and run in shadow mode first.
design_tradeoffs: Per-key ledger increases memory and index overhead; to mitigate we will: compress amort deltas, TTL records after amort_window + grace, and shard-localize hot-key caches while storing cold-key ledger in RocksDB. Alternative of increasing overlap window to avoid double-apply is unacceptable because it increases failover tail latency. We discussed a simpler fix (increment a handshake counter at handoff) but that leaves race conditions if replays arrive out-of-order.
implementation_notes: Core changes touch: enforcement fastpath (edge/enforcer), shard handoff protocol (lease manager), and storage layer (compact ledger store). We'll add unit tests for idempotent apply, integration test driving forced handoff, and a flamegraph-based perf regression test for memory. Key PRs will follow the pattern: storage -> handoff -> enforcement.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature-flagged canary to 10% of tenants on staging (runtime-1.22-canary). Phase 2: 10% production tenants for 24h with close SRE watch. Phase 3: 50% for 48h. Phase 4: 100% rollout and run reconciliation job for remaining affected keys. Each phase requires automated rollback via flag and monitoring thresholds (see below).
qa_criteria: - repro harness no longer shows duplicated amort_record application. - per-key 429 duration reduced to baseline in canary. - memory increase < 12% on enforcers in canary. - reconciliation job marks affected keys and simulates top-up; results validated by metric diffs.
